cards.explanation: The answer is Kadesh-barnea. The text says that after the vast and terrifying wilderness, they reached it. It's also where Moses speaks to them about the hill country. Hang on to that name, friends, because it comes back at the end of the passage.

The answer is False. Moses never tells them to wait for a sign. What he says is, “See, the LORD your God has placed the land before you.” Then comes the order to go up and take possession of it, as the LORD has told them. That's a go-up kind of speech, and I'd be bouncing on my base, ready to roll.

The word is afraid. Moses says, “Do not be afraid or discouraged.” He says it right after telling them the land is placed before them. Fear is the word to watch in this passage, friends. It keeps coming back.

The answer is word on which route and cities to take. The people ask for men who will “…bring us word of what route to follow and which cities to enter.” They want directions, plain and simple. It sounds like a very reasonable ask to me. I'd want a map too, and I'd want it laminated.
The answer is twelve. Moses says, “…I selected twelve men from among you, one from each tribe.” That's one man for every tribe. He also says the plan seemed good to him.

The answer is some of the fruit of the land. The text says, “They took some of the fruit of the land in their hands, carried it down to us…” So the spies don't come back with only words. They bring proof you can hold. It's hard to argue with something you can pick up.

The answer is False. After the report, the people don't head up. Moses says they were unwilling to go up, and he calls it rebelling against the command of the LORD. The spies had said it was a good land, and the people grumbled in their tents anyway. Keep your ears open, friends, because there's more to hear.

The answer is to hand them over to the Amorites. Those are the people's own words. They say the LORD brought them out of Egypt “…to deliver us into the hand of the Amorites to be annihilated.” They say it in their tents, and they begin with, “Because the LORD hates us…” Moses is retelling what they said.

The answer is True. In their grumbling, the people repeat what their brothers said: “The people are larger and taller than we are…” They add that the cities are large, with walls up to the heavens. The people say their brothers made their hearts melt.

The answer is that the LORD goes before them and will fight for them. Moses says, “The LORD your God, who goes before you, will fight for you…” That's the whole reason. It isn't about how strong Israel is. It's about who's walking in front of them.

The answer is as a man carries his son. Moses says the LORD carried them “…as a man carries his son, all the way by which you traveled until you reached this place.” That's a picture of a father and his boy. I like that picture a lot. And Moses says it covers all the way they traveled.

The answer is in fire by night and cloud by day. Fire when it's dark, cloud when it's light, and the LORD goes ahead of them in both. Moses says it's to seek out a place for them to camp and to show them the road to travel. Think about that for a second. Nobody in that camp had to argue about directions.

The answer is True. Moses says the LORD went before them “…to seek out a place for you to camp and to show you the road to travel.” He picked the camping spots and showed the road. That's a lot of care for people who'd soon refuse to trust Him.

The answer is that not one of them will see the good land. The LORD says, “Not one of the men of this evil generation shall see the good land I swore to give your fathers…” That's a hard word, and it comes after He heard their words and grew angry. There's one exception coming, so keep reading.

The word is wholeheartedly. The LORD says Caleb son of Jephunneh will see the land “…because he followed the LORD wholeheartedly.” Wholeheartedly means all in. That's the reason the LORD gives for Caleb. He adds that He will give Caleb and his descendants the land on which he has set foot.

The answer is False. The LORD tells Moses, “Not even you shall enter the land.” Moses says the LORD was angry with him on their account. I think this is a hard thing for him to say out loud, so I'll just let it be heavy for a second.

The word is encourage. Moses is told to cheer on Joshua son of Nun, the man who will carry the next stretch of the job. I think Moses knows what a heavy load feels like. Anybody facing something huge could use someone in their corner, even a stamper with a worn-down handle.

The answer is that they will enter and possess the land. The LORD says these little ones “…will enter the land that I will give them, and they will possess it.” These are the children who, in the people's words, would become captives. They didn't know good from evil on that day. And now the promise lands right on them.

The answer is back to the wilderness toward the Red Sea. The LORD says, “But you are to turn back and head for the wilderness along the route to the Red Sea.” So the direction is back toward the wilderness. I think that's a hard order to hear. A turn-around is a turn-around.

The word is fight. The people say, “We will go up and fight, as the LORD our God has commanded us.” Funny how fast the answer changed, from refusing to go to ready to fight. I think they meant it, but the LORD's command had changed. Their plan didn't match His.

The answer is True. Moses says each man put on his weapons of war, “…thinking it easy to go up into the hill country.” Earlier the people said the cities had walls up to the heavens. Now they think going up is easy, and I think that's quite a swing.

The answer is that the LORD is not with them. He says, “…I am not with you to keep you from defeat by your enemies.” That's the reason He gives for this fight: He is not with them. So He tells them not to go up and fight.

The answer is that they refuse to listen. Moses hands over the LORD's warning and gets nothing back, because the people “…would not listen.” Then up into the hill country they go anyway. It's like hearing the oven timer go off and sliding the cookies back in for one more minute. I think that's a lot of confidence for people who were unwilling to go up earlier in the same story (Deut 1:26).

The answer is that they chase Israel away. Moses says the Amorites “…chased you like a swarm of bees.” They routed Israel from Seir all the way to Hormah. It went just the way the LORD's warning said it would.

The answer is False. The people returned and wept before the LORD, but He would not listen to their voice or give ear to them. That's a hard verse to read. I think it stings, and Moses doesn't dress it up.
